title: Noether's symmetry
lede: A number that never changes while everything else swings: one made-up planet, Earth's two measured moments, then 30,000 simulated moments of 300 orbits sorted by what stays, and 10,000 training states of a tiny network. Part 1 of 3: the idea.

chapters.title: Earth, and a change that changes nothing
What stays fixed in your data?

captions: A made-up planet goes round its sun.
Its distance from the sun swings.
Its speed around the sun swings too.
Multiply them: that bar never moves.
A number that never changes: it is conserved.
Is that real? Take Earth around the Sun.
Closest: 147.095 million km from the Sun.
Its speed there: 30.29 km/s.
Farthest: 152.100 million km.
Its speed there: 29.29 km/s.
Multiply each pair: 4,455.5 and 4,455.0.
Only 0.011 % apart: the same number.
Why is it fixed? Back to our planet.
Its fixed number is called spin.
Its energy never changes either.
Now turn the whole picture round.
Turn it: nothing changes.
That is why spin is conserved.
Start the clock later: nothing changes.
That is why energy is conserved.
A change that changes nothing: a symmetry.
Noether, 1918: each symmetry fixes one number.
Now 300 made-up planets, 100 moments each.
30,000 dots, each where a planet was.
A tangle. The bright dots are our planet.
Now sort every dot by its spin.
Each dot keeps its direction from the sun.
6 shells: one for each spin.
Our planet's 100 dots land on one shell.
As it moves, it slides along its shell.
It never leaves: its spin is fixed.
Now sort the same dots by energy.
Higher up means more energy.
5 layers: one for each energy.
Our planet stays in its layer as it moves.
Two symmetries, two fixed numbers.
Not only planets: a tiny network learning.
100 runs, 100 steps each: 10,000 dots.
Sort them by a sum that should not change.
The same picture: 3 shells.
The weights moved 0.24.
The fixed sum moved 0.00095.
About 250 times less.
Smoke rings too: swap the air, the swirl stays.
Monday: what stays fixed while your data moves?

brand.takeaway: Every symmetry hides something that stays.
